candidate.ask_addressed: Break the writing thread into documented adaptations
candidate.quote: Linear B was deciphered in 1952 by English architect and self-taught linguist Michael Ventris
candidate.summary: Summarises Linear B as adapted from Linear A and deciphered by Ventris in 1952 as Mycenaean Greek: the Minoan-to-Mycenaean script adaptation. The same page says Linear A is undeciphered.
candidate.limits: Encyclopedia summary. I could not open Ventris and Chadwick's 1953 JHS paper or Documents in Mycenaean Greek (paywalled / lending). The adaptation rests on sign-form comparison, not on a text that says so.

reason: strand_unsupported: the quoted sentence (Ventris's 1952 decipherment) says nothing of Linear A or of an adaptation; the strand Linear A -> Mycenaean Greek is stated elsewhere on the page, not in the quote. Wikipedia-only in any case.

candidate.quote: Vocalization of Geʻez occurred in the 4th century, and though the first completely vocalized texts known are inscriptions by Ezana
candidate.summary: Ge'ez derives from Ancient South Arabian, with vocalisation in the 4th century (Ezana; a Wazeba coin has one vocalised letter).
